Boelter changed his plea after the Department of Justice announced it would not seek the death penalty in the case.

By Star Tribune staff

Vance Boelter, who is charged with shooting two Minnesota lawmakers and their families, pleaded guilty on Thursday morning to the attacks.

Boelter had previously pleaded not guilty to the six federal charges tied to the shootings that killed state Rep. Melissa Hortman and her husband, Mark, and injured Sen. John Hoffman and his wife, Yvette.

The hearing comes days after the Justice Department revealed it would not seek the death penalty against Boelter.

After the court hearing, U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen addressed what he called the “scourge” of political violence in America.

“Political violence is a scourge plaguing America in our times,” he said.
